subject: Trading
title: Commodity Exchanges
description: A quick win: understand Commodity Exchanges.

hook.text: The Chicago Board of Trade opened in 1848 so farmers and merchants could lock in grain prices. It still operates today.

buildup.text: Commodity exchanges standardize contracts—grade, quantity, delivery date—so buyers and sellers can trade anonymously.

discovery.text: The CME Group, ICE, and LME are the world's largest. Oil, gold, wheat, and copper all have flagship exchanges.

twist.text: Most exchange volume is now electronic. The famous trading pits where brokers shouted orders are mostly gone.

climax.text: Exchanges provide transparency, liquidity, and counterparty clearing—making commodity trading safer and faster.

punchline.text: A 175-year-old idea still powers global trade.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of a commodity exchange?
options: To standardize contracts and provide transparent, liquid markets
